This application is filed, being aggrieved of the judgement dated 04.04.2018 passed by the Learned Special judge Scheduled Casts and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Mandla in Special S.T.No.200112/2016 whereby appellant has been convicted under Sections 376 (Gha) of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.5,000/-, under Section 342 of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 1 year with fine of Rs.1,000/- and under Section 506-II of IPC and sentence to R.I. for 2 years with fine amount of Rs.1000/-.
3.

entities.text: Scheduled Casts and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Mandla
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted that there are several loopholes in the prosecution story.
Reading from the evidence of the concerned Dr. Malti (PW-5), it is submitted that doctor had given an opinion that she cannot say anything about immediate intercourse.
Another argument is that the age of the prosecutrix was major and she was a consenting party.
In this regard, evidence of father of the prosecutrix (PW-2) is read over.
Similarly, it is submitted that Chironji Bai (PW-3) has also not supported the prosecution 2 CRA-3366-2018 case.
4. Shri Nitin Gupta- Deputy Government Advocate supports impugned judgement.
5. After hearing learned counsel for appellant, it is evident that in Para-7 of cross-examination of PW-2, by all permutation and combination, the age of the victim comes out to be a minor.

Similarly,
doctor has not given opinion about any immediate sexual intercourse but FSL report (Exhibit- P/25)
reveals that on slide (Exhibit B), there were large spots of semen and human sperms were found.
Thus, when these facts are taken into consideration, then the appellant has failed to prove that the victim was a major and consenting party, hence no indulgence is called for.
6. Accordingly, the application fails and is dismissed.
